name: Chain-of-Thought (Chain Aggregation)
definition: Post-hoc aggregation over the N council member answers: each member is called once; the structure is built from the returned reasoning text and makes 0 LLM calls of its own. Chain: members' steps collapsed into one ordered chain.
selected_in: POST /api/council/run reasoning_mode (LLM Lab, research only); Training Wizard: restored voting configs only
persisted_in: council transcript; Training Wizard council_config (not consumed in training)
affects_final: Boosts the confidence of the member it prefers by ×1.15 before voting. Under the default 'vote' strategy the winner is the largest answer group (confidence only breaks ties and picks the answer text); under 'confidence', 'consensus' and 'debate' the boost can change the winner.
prod_observed: council route ran once in production; mode not recorded in the audit counts
benchmark: reasoning-strategies harness: mock only (6 configs × 5 tasks)
result: NOT_RUN with a real provider in this repo; the mock shows ≈3× calls/tokens for chain/tree/graph *prompting* variants — not this aggregation.
limitations: Training Wizard stored council_config.reasoning_mode and kind='voting' with the run, but the training path never runs the voting council: only kind='proposer_judge' is consumed (model_training._maybe_council_override) and use_got only adds a preprocessing trace graph. Since 2026-11-14 the standard wizard offers Proposer / Judge only; restored voting configs are kept and labelled research only. Not iterative CoT prompting; raw chain-of-thought is never stored.
next_step: Done 2026-11-14: hidden from the standard Training Wizard, research only in LLM Lab. Measure in notebook 02 before any re-productisation.

name: Council (multi-persona / multi-model vote)
definition: N members (personas or providers) answer once; aggregation (cot/tot/got/none) then a voting strategy.
affects_final: advisory answer on the council page; does not change a training run
prod_observed: 1 council run in production (3 member calls)
result: Pre-registered 110 cases (71 scored): best single model 70/71; no council condition beat it (all six REJECTED_ON_THIS_BENCHMARK); some variants 69/71. Always-on councils: 3–4 calls, 2.7–4.5× tokens, up to 2.3× latency (judge), up to 2.5× provider cost. The semantic critic was right and outvoted on feature_screening:29 and :34 — majority vote discarded the useful dissent. Gain correlated with error diversity (double-fault −0.83), not provider count.
calibration: Brier reported per condition in RESULTS.md
limitations: Ceiling effect (70/71); product endpoint, Validator and tenant context were not part of the benchmark; any claim beyond this set is UNKNOWN.
next_step: Only as a risk/uncertainty escalation candidate; follow-up pre-registration on a harder set (council_followup_headroom_preregistration).

name: Jev bounded decisions (typed, closed-set)
definition: External typed decision provider over a declared candidate set; Athena checks every answer against the set.
selected_in: decision-engine provider eligibility; tenant policy jev_mode
affects_final: only when a tenant sets jev_mode=PRODUCTION_ELIGIBLE (default DISABLED); then the resolver still applies policy
policy: jev_mode DISABLED by default; EXPERIMENTAL is never production-eligible
result: EXECUTION_SCALE (n=90): accuracy 0.578 → 0.733, Brier 0.576 → 0.364 with typed semantics; 95% Wilson intervals overlap.
limitations: One decision family, one model; vendor dependency; shadow-mode comparison against the router not built.
